title: Ed Kirkeby, Fats's business manager
summary: Autrey hesitantly calls Kirkeby a capable business man who almost owned Victor but was not on Autrey's personal side.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: That's when Ed Kirkaby came in?
Ho, yeah, well Ed came in then.
(Laughs.) Well, Herman, tell us about Ed Kirkaby.
Well, he's a very nice man. I mean, oh my, should I? Do I?
Oh, well. I mean, Ed's a nice guy.
Oh, God! Well no, no. Ed's all right. (Laughs.) You dropped me that time. You laid one on me, baby.
(Laughs.) Well, we'll get around to that one in a little while.
Well now Fats had Ed to take care of his business, some business for him, for him, and Ed moved in
there to -- smooth operator. He was working for Victor. Victor had to let him go. He almost owned Victor.
And a couple of other places he worked he almost owned them. Ed's Ed, I mean, you know.
He's a great -- he's a good business man.
You damn right. He's a capable --
A good guy to have on your side.
On your side. Was he -- well, you could feel he wasn't always on your side.
